channel.title: Food Safety Magazine - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Food Safety Magazine (food-safety.com)

item.title: FDA to Hold Public Meeting on Scope of Dietary Supplement Ingredients
item.description: The March 27 hybrid event will discuss new methodologies to produce existing dietary ingredients and specific ingredient types, including proteins, enzymes, and microbials, within the scope of the Dietary Supplement Health and Education Act of 1994.

item.title: What Food Safety KPIs Say About Food Safety Culture—Part 2
item.description: This article further discusses the results of a survey of food processors worldwide regarding food safety culture and the key performance indicators (KPIs) used to measure daily operations and continuous improvement.

item.title: Study Uses AI to Screen Milk Samples for Mycotoxin Contamination
item.description: The researchers positioned the machine learning model as a low-cost complement to traditional testing workflows, helping dairy processors enhance food safety while targeting laboratory resources.

item.title: Monadnock’s Compostable Card Achieves TÜV OK Home Compost Certification
item.description: Intended as a single-use plastic replacement, the sustainable material is FDA food contact-compliant, moisture-resistant, and temperature-stable.

item.title: RFK Jr. Says Federal Ultra-Processed Foods Definition is Coming in April
item.description: In his remarks on a recent Joe Rogan Experience podcast episode, Secretary Kennedy also suggested FDA is considering a new approach to front-of-pack nutrition labeling.

item.title: SQF Food Safety Code Edition 10 Arrives in a Digital-First Format
item.description: Marking the first time an SQF Code is introduced as a fully digital experience, the newly released Edition 10 is designed to strengthen audit credibility, reinforce food safety culture, and provide clearer signals around risk.

item.title: Study Identifies Critical Temperature Threshold During Food Processing to Inactivate Norovirus
item.description: Maximum reductions in norovirus infectivity occurred rapidly once temperatures reached 60 °C (140 °F). The findings could help inform improved thermal processing recommendations for foodborne norovirus.

item.title: FoodSafe Drains Launches Drainage Evaluation Program for Food Facilities
item.description: The engineering-led assessment program helps food and beverage processors identify drainage risks, prioritize hygienic upgrades, and implement facility-specific standard operating procedures (SOPs) for long-term performance.

item.title: Hillbrush Transitions Hygiene Range to Plastic Free Packaging Amid Rising PFAS Restrictions
item.description: Hillbrush Transitions Hygiene Range to Plastic Free Packaging Amid Rising PFAS Restrictions

item.title: FDA Releases Initial Findings from Foodborne Pathogen Study in California Growing Region
item.description: The California Longitudinal Study, a five-year environmental study of California’s Central Coast produce-growing region, identified wildlife, livestock, and surface water as potential contributors to the persistence and movement of Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC).
